sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why mitzvos must be performed each specific day, given that prayer can refine and elevate mitzvos from adjacent days.

translations.translation: However, this explanation only explains the connection of mitzvos to days.
But it is still not understood the necessity of performing the mitzvos specifically each day,
for seemingly,
even if one misses one day and the next day performs two mitzvos,
the mitzvos will be refined through the prayer of the following day.
And one cannot say that prayer can refine and elevate only the mitzvos belonging to that day,
for there is no reason for this distinction.
Moreover, since there is the concept of completion
(on the following day,
in the prayer adjacent to it)58
"And we do not say that since its day has passed, its offering is void"59,
and even that
(regarding the intention of prayer)
one prayer gathered from the prayers of the entire year elevates the prayers of the entire year60,
this implies also regarding the elevation of mitzvos through prayer,
that prayer elevates even the mitzvos of the adjacent day, etc.
And a support for this matter – the prayers of Shabbos, which elevate the prayers of all the weekdays along with all the Torah and good deeds included in them61.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the purpose of mitzvos is to refine the physical world, including time itself, necessitating a mitzvah each day.

translations.translation: But the matter is,
behold it is known that the purpose of Torah and mitzvos is to effect clarification and refinement in this physical world.
For this is what "Torah is not in heaven"62 means,
and all Torah was given to make peace in the world63,
and all the more so mitzvos, which were only given to refine the creations through them64.
And even the mitzvah of tzedakah is equivalent to all the mitzvos
(and is called by the name "mitzvah" in general),
for the purpose of mitzvos
[and likewise the purpose of the soul's descent below]
which is
[not for the sake of the soul, but rather]
in order to rectify the body and the Nefesh HaBahamis and its portion in the world,
is completed through the mitzvah of tzedakah
(more so than through all other mitzvos),
as explained in Tanya65.
And this is66
that there must be specifically complete days,
that on each and every day there must be the fulfillment of a mitzvah,
for since the definition of the world is place and time67,
behold it is understood that Torah and mitzvos
(whose purpose is to rectify the world)
must also rectify time.
Therefore it is necessary that on every day there be the performance of a mitzvah
(even though when one misses one day he can make the garment by fulfilling two mitzvos tomorrow),
for in order to rectify the days68
(time)
itself, it is necessary that each69
and every day do its work.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Avraham was old, coming in days" refers to the superior level of rectifying time itself, completing the purpose of a dwelling place in the lower worlds.

translations.translation: And this is "And Avraham was old, coming in days",
that after "Avraham was old" he is also "coming in days," which is a greater level even than the level of "old."
For behold, the true intention in the creation of the worlds
(in the aspect of Atzmus Ein Sof)
is that which the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place specifically in the lower realms70.
And this intention is completed through the service of man,
"You are called 'man'"71,
that specifically man can complete this intention.
And this is why he is called by the name "Adam",
on account of the two extremes: that he is "similar to the upper one"72
and that he was formed from the earth73,
that his body was made from the earth itself74
and in a manner that it was initially inert by itself
(without any living soul within it)
and as it is written75
"Your eyes saw my unformed body"
(and not like the body of a plant or animal)76,
for also this matter in the description of "man"
(on account of the earth)
indicates his superiority77,
that he clarifies, rectifies, and elevates even the inert, which is the lowest, below which there is no lower.
And this level within him is actualized specifically through the service of "coming in days."
For through the service of "old"
(itself),
even though through it he also clarified and rectified his portion in the world
(place),
nevertheless,
since he has not yet rectified time,
behold he has not yet completed the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms.
Therefore, even though this service reaches the aspect of Atik Yomin,
which is in abstraction
(and separation)
from the aspect of days,
this is not the ultimate perfection.
However, through the service of "coming in days"78,
when one works to rectify the days,
and even to the extent of "and I will fill the number of your days"79
"number" from the term "sapphire stone"
(and as explained in Torah Ohr80
that "the number of your days" is like "the heavens declare"81
which the Zohar82 interprets
as shining, sparkling, and sapphire-like),
meaning that man illuminates the days
(time)
with the light of Torah and mitzvos,
through this he completes the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms
(in the lowest of this world itself83),
and this
(the completion of this intention)
is the ultimate perfection of man's level,
as above.
